correctness.rationale: Positive unilateral shift weights give exact weighted-shift singular values; iteration applies the binomial smoothing kernel to log weights. Binomial concentration proves the fixed-parameter norm scale and locally uniform normalized singular profile. For alpha>1 the lower derivative bound alpha*j yields a fixed summable majorant and dominated convergence. Alpha=1 evaluates to an exact geometric series. For 0<alpha<1 a uniformly convergent derivative on j=O(n^(1-alpha)) gives the exponential profile, and two separate tail estimates (j<=n and j>n) give tightness for an infinite Riemann sum, yielding t^(1-alpha)/(pc alpha). The conclusion holds for all fixed p>0, including the quasi-norm regime. Source check.py passed 582 finite assertions; those are diagnostics, not the asymptotic proof.

value.rationale: The intrinsic normalized Schatten mass measures how many singular modes remain significant when the operator norm tends to zero. The work completely distinguishes rank-one concentration (alpha>1), fixed geometric spectral mass (alpha=1), and a diverging effective-rank boundary layer with sharp coefficient and full limiting profile (0<alpha<1) in a natural stretched-exponential family. The exact phase boundary is the standard exponential weight and the change of behavior is invisible to qualitative Schatten convergence. This yields a meaningful structural classification rather than an arbitrary finite computation or a routine parameter substitution.
